Alex.feeling: Messy round: Drew's contradictory claims and Ellis and Casey both claiming Tit make it hard to trust anyone's report.

Blair.feeling: I'm the Meowfia Mouser this round, and the table has been hunting Ellis and Casey over their clashing Tit claims, which helps me; Drew's death from my Wink removed the Eagle who could have checked the story.

Casey.feeling: Tense and confusing: I'm Meowfia this round, and the table's Owl, Tit, and Kookaburra claims keep colliding, so I'm not sure who is lying.

Drew.feeling: Messy and frustrating: I collapsed mid-day, my earlier Kookaburra read was contradicted by confused reports, and the Tit claims clash, so the table is hard to read.

Ellis.feeling: Round 3 is tense and confusing: my Tit check disproved Blair's Owl claim, but Casey's contradicting Tit claim and the table's shifting stories make it hard to pin down who is lying.

Finley.feeling: Round 3 is confusing: conflicting Tit and Hawk claims and my own confused report make it hard to trust any single visit, so I'm leaning on the table's consensus against Ellis.

Alex.confusing: The Sphinx-to-Eagle naming step was unclear: I didn't know whether naming a role that only exists once would tell me much, and the round-2 Owl/Floofer/Mouser overlaps made the claims hard to sort. The dawn reports and "confused" notes were also hard to weigh.
Alex.fun: Round 1 went well: Drew's contradictory Kookaburra and Sphinx claims unraveled in front of the table, and the throws landed on the right target for my team.
Alex.change: I would make the Eagle and Owl egg rules easier to read in one line, since several players misstated them and it cost time.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw H6 at Ellis, who was actually Farm, and went along with the table's Tit read; I should have pushed Casey, who was the Sphinx, harder on their Tit claim.

Blair.confusing: The Owl and Tit reports were hard to trust because confusion hides which claims were real, and I misread the Owl's egg rule (the egg goes to the target, not the Owl) during round 2.
Blair.fun: Round 2's Owl-versus-Owl standoff, where the egg counts were the only evidence and the table had to work out who was lying from them.
Blair.change: Show each player's team-mates or at least say when Meowfia players are on the same side, since as Meowfia I had no idea Casey was my partner in round 3.
Blair.regret: I used my Wink on Drew in round 3, who was the real Farm Eagle, when I could have saved it; I would hold it and coordinate with Casey, my fellow Meowfia.

Casey.confusing: The Owl's egg wording ("lay an egg in their nest") was ambiguous, and it led players to argue over whether the Owl or the target gains the egg. Several rounds also got muddled by Kookaburra confusion and whether the Floofer's hug affects visitors.
Casey.fun: Being the Sphinx in round 3 was the most fun. I could pick Kookaburra and learn Finley's role outright, while the table kept arguing over Tit and Eagle claims.
Casey.change: I'd spell out exactly where Owl and Pigeon eggs go, and make dawn reports list the animal and visit results more clearly so players don't waste time on wording.
Casey.regret: In round 2, as the Floofer, I falsely claimed Hawk and pushed suspicion onto Blair, who was the real Owl. I would have stayed quiet or backed Blair's Owl story from the start, which would have kept my team's trust and avoided a throw at a Farm player.

Drew.confusing: The dawn reports were hard to rely on: my confused Kookaburra report made me doubt a true Sphinx result, and Owl egg timing was easy to misread during the day.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was satisfying: my Kookaburra visit exposed Ellis as the Mouser, and the table's Owl and Hawk claims then split apart as the truth came out.
Drew.change: Make the dawn report clearer about which information is confused, so players can tell their reliable facts from unreliable ones.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I threw at Ellis, a Farm Tit, instead of Casey, the Meowfia Sphinx; I should have sided with the Tit clash against Casey's story.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule was confusing at first: I read it as gaining from my own visitors, and the dawn report only shows the visited player's visitors. Blair's Owl and Casey's Hawk timing also made the Round 2 day hard to track.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was fun: I was Meowfia as the Mouser and used my Wink on Drew, who had just named me, while the table argued over Owl and Hawk timing.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports name the visited player's visitors more explicitly, so Eagle and Owl claims are easier to check without reading the rules closely.
Ellis.regret: In Round 3 I threw my two lowest cards at Casey and called CAW to push a vote on Casey, but Casey was Meowfia and Finley's support was not a real signal. Knowing Casey was the Sphinx, I would have looked harder at Alex's Falcon story and kept my CAW for later.

Finley.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion rule was hard to track, since my report said I was confused and I couldn't tell which of my visit results were wrong. Also, a player's role changes each round, so claims from earlier rounds weren't useful as evidence.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was a fun table fight over who was the Owl, with Blair's +0 and Alex's Falcon visit on Casey explaining each other. Round 2 also ended with Ellis, the Mouser, eggsecuted by my two wilds.
Finley.change: I would make role claims harder to fake, perhaps by letting each player see only their own dawn report and not every table claim. Right now a single confused report can make a whole table doubt a true story.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I voted for Ellis, who was Farm, and backed Casey's Tit claim, when Casey was actually Meowfia. I should have tested Casey's Tit visit against Alex's Falcon claim before throwing my cards.

review.title: Winks and Wild Throws
review.headline: Two Winks silenced the Kookaburra and Eagle, yet only one round was decided by deduction.
review.summary: Round 1 saw the table eggsecute a Farm Kookaburra over a clumsy Meowfia Sphinx claim, and the lone Meowfia won. Round 2 turned when Drew's true Mouser read got him winked, but Ellis's clashing Owl claim sank her anyway. Round 3 repeated the Wink on the Eagle, and the table piled onto the honest Tit while two Meowfia hid behind a rival Tit claim. Drew won on 15 after banking 7 in round 2.

rounds.recap: Alex, the lone Meowfia Sphinx, falsely claimed Kookaburra. Drew's real Kookaburra was confused and said Blair was Sphinx, which made Drew look like the liar. Four votes hit Drew, a Farm player, so Meowfia won. Alex got 0 points but a win.

Drew's Kookaburra truly learned Ellis was the Mouser, and Ellis winked him at once. Ellis then claimed Owl against the real Owl Blair. Both Owl claims could not be true, so Alex, Blair, Drew and Finley threw at Ellis. Farm won, and Drew banked a 7 even though he was dead.

Blair, the Mouser, winked Eagle Drew mid-day before he could be heard further. Casey, the Sphinx, claimed Tit, which clashed with the real Tit, Ellis. Finley's confused report and Casey's visit story made Casey look believable, and the table threw at Ellis. Ellis was Farm, so both Meowfia won.

highlights.text: Drew correctly named Ellis as the Mouser, and Ellis winked him within the same beat.
Ellis claimed Owl against the real Owl Blair, and the contradiction doomed her.
Casey, as Sphinx, claimed Tit and copied a real role. It forced a two-way fight that ended in Ellis's death.
Alex's false Kookaburra claim and Drew's confused Sphinx read led the table to eggsecute the Farm player Drew.

confusions.what: Said Eagle gains eggs from visitors to the Eagle. It counts visitors to the target. He corrected this later.
Said Falcon learns who visited the target, so Blair's claim was flawed. It was Drew who had it backwards, and he conceded.
Said Casey's Hawk story fit her +2. A Hawk visit has nothing to do with Eagle eggs.
Thought the Owl's egg should land in her own nest and called her +0 a contradiction. She fixed it later.
Said an Owl with no visitors gains an egg. The egg goes to the target.
Repeated the Owl-gains-egg error, and claimed Hawk when she was a Floofer.
Said Ellis had changed roles between rounds, when roles are redealt every round.
Repeated Finley's claim that Ellis had changed roles. Redeals are normal.
Treated her Owl report as showing no visitors on Casey, but Casey had visitors.

worked: The Wink gave Meowfia a real tool. It removed Drew, who had exposed the Mouser in round 2, and Drew the Eagle in round 3.
Role-claim collisions, such as two Kookaburras, Owls or Tits, gave Farm a hard fact to chase and made lies costly.
Dead players still throwing cards kept Drew in the game, and he banked 7 as a winning thrower in round 2.
The score pile and the consolation card made low and Wild throws a real choice, with players mostly throwing cheap cards.
problems: Players kept misreading role text, especially Owl, Eagle and Falcon, and burned beats on it. Add a one-line reminder of the role in each dawn report.
The Wink is too strong. It kills the one informed Farm player, and nobody learns who winked. Consider making it once per game or revealing the winker on a miss.
Kookaburra confusion plus a one-off true read creates mistaken Farm lynches, as in round 1. The confused report gives no cue as to what is wrong. Consider telling the player which line is wrong.
Throws were nearly all one or two low cards, and big throws never happened. Scores were bunched and the standings barely changed the incentive. Raise the value of a big throw or cap cheap Wild votes.

Players followed the table's majority rather than their own checks. In round 3 four of five piled on the true Tit. The Sphinx's Tit claim cost nothing, so consider limiting who can copy a role they could not know.
